The EU AI Act complements existing regulatory frameworks, including data protection requirements under the GDPR. It applies without prejudice to these requirements, meaning that when AI systems process personal data, the GDPR remains fully applicable, particularly concerning automated decisions with significant effects, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, and privacy by design.

The AI Act introduces further, risk-based obligations that depend on the role of the company (provider or deployer) and the risk class of the AI system. For high-risk systems, companies must conduct risk assessments, maintain documentation, and adhere to transparency obligations. Users must be able to recognize when they are interacting with an AI system, and those creating synthetic media must label it appropriately. Additionally, the Act emphasizes the need for AI literacy among users to ensure they can effectively operate AI systems.

Overall, the AI Act establishes a framework that integrates transparency obligations with data protection requirements, ensuring that companies are accountable for the use of AI while safeguarding individuals' rights.
